proof:
1. (Basis.) a and e are orthonormal, hence linearly independent; span{a, e} ⊆ Q has dimension 2 = dim Q, so span{a, e} = Q.
2. (Parametrization.) Define ι : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ^P, ι(v) := v₀a + v₁e. ι is linear and |ι v|² = v₀²|a|² + 2v₀v₁⟨a, e⟩ + v₁²|e|² = v₀² + v₁² = |v|², so ι is norm preserving, hence an isometry (|ι v − ι v'| = |ι(v − v')| = |v − v'|). Its range is span{a, e} = Q (step 1), and ⟨ι v, a⟩ = v₀, ⟨ι v, e⟩ = v₁.
3. (Transfer to Lebesgue measure.) For every S ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∩ Q = ι(ι^{-1}(S)) because range ι = Q. By isometry invariance of the Euclidean Hausdorff measure (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and μHE[2] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume 2): μHE[2](S ∩ Q) = μHE[2](ι^{-1}(S)) = vol₂(ι^{-1}(S)). If S is measurable, ν₀(S) = μHE[2](S ∩ Q) (Measure.restrict_apply), so ν₀(S) = vol₂(ι^{-1}(S)).
4. (Finite on compacts.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. K is closed, hence measurable, and K ⊆ B̄(0, ρ) for some ρ ≥ 0. Since ι preserves norms, ι^{-1}(K) ⊆ B̄(0, ρ) ⊆ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), so ν₀(K) = vol₂(ι^{-1}(K)) ≤ vol₂(B̄(0, ρ)) < ∞. Hence ν₀ is finite on compact sets. (Equivalently, and shortest in Lean: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule applied to finrank Q = 2 shows that ν₀ is a regular measure, and every regular measure is finite on compact sets.)
5. (Open square.) Let 0 ≤ r ≤ 2 and S := {w : |w| < 3, |⟨w, a⟩| < r, |⟨w, e⟩| < r}, an open (so measurable) set. By step 2, ι^{-1}(S) = {v : |v| < 3, |v₀| < r, |v₁| < r} = {v : |v₀| < r, |v₁| < r}, since |v₀|, |v₁| < r implies |v|² = v₀² + v₁² < 2r² ≤ 8 < 9. The measurable equivalence EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → (Fin 2 → ℝ), v ↦ (v₀, v₁), is volume preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), and it maps this set onto the box (−r, r) × (−r, r) = Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo (−r) r), whose volume is ofReal(2r)·ofReal(2r) = ofReal(4r²) (Real.volume_pi_Ioo). Hence ν₀(S) = ofReal(4r²). (For r = 0 both sides are 0.)
6. (Closed square.) Let K_r := {w : |w| ≤ 3, |⟨w, a⟩| ≤ r, |⟨w, e⟩| ≤ r}, a closed (so measurable) set. As in step 5, ι^{-1}(K_r) = {v : |v₀| ≤ r, |v₁| ≤ r} (because |v|² ≤ 2r² ≤ 8 ≤ 9), which corresponds to the box [−r, r]² = Icc (fun _ => −r) (fun _ => r) of volume ofReal(2r)·ofReal(2r) = ofReal(4r²) (Real.volume_Icc_pi). Hence ν₀(K_r) = ofReal(4r²). ∎
key_steps: (a, e) is an orthonormal basis of Q, so ι(v) = v₀a + v₁e is an isometry of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) onto Q with ⟨ι v, a⟩ = v₀, ⟨ι v, e⟩ = v₁.
For measurable S, ν₀(S) = μHE[2](ι(ι^{-1}S)) = vol₂(ι^{-1}S) (isometry invariance; μHE[2] = volume in dimension 2).
For compact K, ι^{-1}K is bounded, so ν₀(K) < ∞.
For 0 ≤ r ≤ 2 the ball constraint is redundant on Q (2r² ≤ 8 < 9), so the preimages are the boxes (−r, r)² and [−r, r]², of volume 4r².
